name: radical
label: Research: learned endpoints, retained replies and compressed plans

terminal_rules.label: Actual checkmate for the solver
Actual mate against us or stalemate

HEURISTIC reserve king retreats for advanced pawn defense: abandon a noncapturing king retreat in a pawn ending when no enemy pawn has reached its sixth or seventh rank; a tempo preference, not a forced-loss claim

HEURISTIC defend an enemy passer before a remote pawn push: when behind after recovering material, abandon a quiet pawn move that does not outrun the enemy king while our king still attacks no enemy nonrook pawn; a defensive tempo preference

HEURISTIC premature pawn race after recovery: abandon a quiet nonpassed pawn dash outside the enemy king square after a material gain unless our king already attacks a nonrook enemy pawn; a tempo preference, not a forced-loss claim

HEURISTIC losing pawn race: while down material, abandon a pawn ending where an enemy passer outruns our king and we have no passer outside the enemy king square; a race preference, not a forced-loss proof

EXPERIMENTAL queenless unattacked capture reserve: gain a minor-piece lead with an unattacked piece capture and king flights off one line; every enemy capture permits legal recapture, no capture wins attacker value, every check permits favorable checker capture and no promotion is available
HEURISTIC backward king drift: abandon a noncapturing king retreat when there is no enemy passed pawn and neither king is checked; a move preference, not a forced-loss claim

EXPERIMENTAL defended queen counterattack reserve: gained at least a minor piece, a defended queen attack and king flights off one line; no enemy capture wins attacker value before recapture, every enemy capture permits recapture, and every check permits favorable checker capture; quiet counterattack only

EXPERIMENTAL active king and pawn compensation: after a gain restores equal pawns, push a pawn toward our king while it attacks the only nonrook enemy pawn; our king reaches an own pawn no later, with no immediate capture, enemy promotion or near-king pawn weakness

EXPERIMENTAL protected passed-pawn race after recovery: equal pawn material after a gain, the advanced passer is defended and outruns the enemy king, whose sole nonrook pawn does not outrun ours; no immediate enemy capture or promotion
HEURISTIC unsafe pawn dash: a quiet nonpassed pawn outside the enemy king square is attacked and undefended, and an enemy capture has no legal recapture; abandon this pawn dash

EXPERIMENTAL checking promotion recovery: gain material and reach a positive reserve by promotion, give check with an unattacked promoted piece and a mobile king; no immediate enemy capture, checking reply or promotion

LEARNED advancing king-supported passer: advance a passer toward our king controlling its promotion square, with gained pawn surplus and own king no farther from the pawn; no enemy passer, capture or check

LEARNED king-supported passer: gained a pawn surplus with our king controlling an own pawn promotion square and no farther from a friendly pawn; the enemy king is at least as central, with no enemy passer, capture or check

LEARNED breakthrough passer: advance a passer on a clear promotion file before any enemy piece can geometrically intercept it; no immediate enemy capture, check or promotion, and defer a ready promotion unless material has improved
LEARNED ready breakthrough after a material gain: clear promotion route beats every geometric enemy interception, with no immediate enemy forcing move

LEARNED open-line capture reserve: gain at least a minor piece after a piece capture opens a line; every enemy capture trades down and permits recapture, every check permits favorable checker capture, and there is no enemy promotion

LEARNED open-line surplus reserve: gain at least a minor piece after a piece capture opens a line; the surplus exceeds the largest legal capture, king flights are not aligned, every capture permits recapture, every check permits favorable checker capture, and there is no promotion

LEARNED defensive pawn recovery: after recovering material, a nonadvancing king attacks a nonrook enemy pawn with a race margin and outside pawn diversion; no enemy capture, promotion or passer outside our king square

LEARNED queenless king-battery pressure: improved material, a friendly slider battery faces the enemy king, the mover is unattacked or defended, every opposing capture has a legal recapture, and no check or promotion is available

LEARNED improved-material pawn pressure: an unattacked passed-pawn advance defends loose material, a passer outruns the opposing king and our king escapes off one line; material improved, no enemy queen or immediate promotion
LEARNED promotion after material gain: low material, gained two points, an unattacked pawn can promote and a passer outruns the enemy king; no immediate enemy check or promotion
LEARNED connected seventh-rank passers: an unattacked passer can promote abreast of a friendly pawn, our king escapes do not share one queen line, and the opponent has no queen or immediate promotion
LEARNED supported pawn break: equal pawn ending, defended pawn stands abreast of a friendly pawn, more central king guards a safe blocked pawn, and no enemy passer

LEARNED supported line pressure: material improved, a defended mover attacks higher material and opens a line; every opposing capture has a legal recapture and no immediate check or promotion is available
LEARNED material gain with a forced interposition: our improved material lead is maintained while the opponent must block a check and has no capture or promotion
LEARNED forced queen concession after a rook recapture: every check evasion interposes a queen on a square with no geometric defender; no own queen

LEARNED favorable defender exchange: capture a higher-value defender and gain positive material that survives the largest legal capture; no favorable enemy capture or promotion, and every enemy check permits a favorable capture of its checker
LEARNED queenless exchange lead after king recapture: gained positive material survives all geometrically attacked material, king has three flights, and opponent has no immediate capture or promotion

LEARNED guarded king after material gain: positive lead survives one legal capture, both queens remain, king is defended and unattacked with flights off one line; no favorable enemy capture or promotion

LEARNED queen-and-rook initiative at equal material: queen is near the enemy king, and an unattacked defended rook checks and restricts that king; own king has three flights and opponent has no capture, promotion or seventh-rank pawn

LEARNED queenless rook activity at least equal material: recover material with an unattacked rook taking a defender, attack a loose target, and keep at least three king flights; no favorable enemy capture or promotion

LEARNED queenless capture reserve: gain at least two points with a minor-piece lead by capturing the queen, king mobile, no enemy immediate promotion; continue while the opponent has a check; no favorable enemy capture
LEARNED queenless material reserve after an unattacked queen capture: positive improved material exceeds any one legal capture and king has a flight; all enemy checks permit favorable checker capture
LEARNED retained queen reserve after an unattacked queen capture: positive improved material exceeds any one legal capture and king has off-line flights
LEARNED pawn recapture advantage: restore equal pawns by a king recapture, with a flank entry ahead of the enemy king and no enemy passer or forcing move

LEARNED rook-check initiative after a material gain: our queen is within two king steps of the enemy king, checking rook is defended and unattacked, no friendly nonpawn piece is attacked, and no enemy capture, promotion or passed pawn; an advantage heuristic, not a forced-mate proof
LEARNED new-pin pressure advantage: create an outnumbered absolute pin with an unattacked mover and no immediate enemy forcing move

EXPERIMENTAL queenless cheaper-piece queen capture: unattacked capturer, positive reserve after the largest legal capture and king flights off one line; neither queen remains and no enemy check or promotion or passed-pawn race

LEARNED pin and loose-material advantage: equal material, a defended new higher-piece pin and an attack on loose material; no enemy promotion, every enemy check offers an equal-or-cheaper checker capture, and every enemy capture offers a legal recapture

EXPERIMENTAL protected checking gain: ahead after gaining material, defended check that captures or leaves its mover unattacked, and king flights off one line; no immediate enemy capture, check or promotion

EXPERIMENTAL forcing capture reserve: gain nonqueen material with a minor-piece lead beyond one legal capture; give check or attack the queen, and every enemy check permits an equal-or-cheaper checker capture
LEARNED pawn-ending recovery: regain equality, restrict the enemy king and approach a pawn flank; no enemy passed pawn, check or capture
LEARNED promotion pressure: protected attack on a promotion blocker in low material, with an outside-square passer and no immediate enemy check, promotion or capture escaping recapture
LEARNED pawn advantage against a passer: extra pawn after defending a loose pawn; no immediate enemy promotion
LEARNED first-promotion advantage: the moved pawn can legally promote next and outruns the enemy king in a pawn-only ending; the opponent has no immediate check or promotion
LEARNED queen exchange: pawn takes the last queen into a safe surplus; no passed-pawn race or fully locked enemy pawn structure

EXPERIMENTAL secured middlegame gain: opposing queen remains, our king has three flights, no current check or equal-or-cheaper capture, and every capturing piece can legally be recaptured; defer a king move to the checking-response rule
EXPERIMENTAL secured middlegame king capture: original material reserve and no available enemy checking reply

EXPERIMENTAL queenless material advantage: gained a minor-piece lead, king has escapes off one line, every enemy capture permits a legal recapture, and no friendly nonpawn piece is attacked; the moved piece is unattacked
LEARNED pawn race advantage: equal or extra material, our passer outruns its king, and no enemy passer outruns ours; defer lone nonrook-pawn opposition until the seventh rank
LEARNED pawn advantage: advanced king reaches an own pawn no later than the enemy king, after a quiet move with a reserve exceeding one legal capture and no enemy passer
LEARNED pawn infiltration: attack a nonrook pawn with a flank race margin, on both wings, after a material gain or restricting the opposing king, with no enemy passer
EXPERIMENTAL guarded pawn infiltration: king attacks a nonrook pawn with race margin and guards a blocking pawn; material is equal or ahead; no enemy passer
EXPERIMENTAL tactical recovery: gained to equality with a defended checking skewer and no legal enemy capture
EXPERIMENTAL pawn reserve: safe lead on both wings, more central king, no enemy passer or completely locked enemy pawns
EXPERIMENTAL material advantage: gained at least two points, lead at least a minor piece, lead exceeds all attacked material, and our king and its legal flights are not confined to one queen line
EXPERIMENTAL queen material advantage: gained material exceeds all attacked exposure, with our queen and at least three legal king flights

Improved positive material outside a pawn-only ending; opponent has no check, capture or promotion; no sixth-rank enemy pawn and every promotion allows a favorable legal capture; no defended promotion square
EXPERIMENTAL tactical recovery: material restored to equality after gaining at least two points; opponent has no check, capture or promotion or passed pawn
Own move after an exchange: lead exceeds all currently attacked material
EXPERIMENTAL favorable pawn ending: secured gain, two wings, more central king; no passed-pawn race, doubled-pawn surplus or near-king pawn weakness
LEARNED checking queen capture: our queen reserve survives a legal recapture and our king has flights off one line
Bounded queen reserve: improved minor-piece lead covers any single capture, our king has a flight, and no capture of a strictly more valuable piece is available
Bounded quiet queen reserve: improved minor-piece lead covers any single capture, our king has a flight, and the opponent has no checking move

Secured material; every check permits a legal capture of its checker by an equal-or-cheaper piece; no sixth-rank enemy pawn and every promotion allows a favorable legal capture; no defended promotion square
Checking capture secures gained material; every legal evasion is noncapturing and nonchecking
EXPERIMENTAL locked-pawn ending: safe blocker, clear escort corridor and near-side king with direct race lead
EXPERIMENTAL locked-pawn ending: safe blocker and clear escort corridor; near-side or guarding king plus outside-pawn diversion
EXPERIMENTAL locked-pawn ending: safe blocker and clear escort corridor; near-side or guarding king plus outside-pawn diversion

LEARNED defended extra-piece reserve: gained a minor-piece lead exceeding any single legal capture; our king has flights off one line, every enemy capture permits a legal recapture, and no enemy check or promotion is available
EXPERIMENTAL captured queen reserve: a cheaper piece captures the queen, minor-piece lead survives any legal capture, our queen remains, our king has a flight, and no seventh-rank enemy pawn

LEARNED protected recapture advantage: gained at least two points and either a minor-piece lead or surplus exceeding any legal capture; moved piece defended, king mobile, enemy captures recapturable, no enemy check, favorable capture or promotion

LEARNED defended promotion-blocker attack: ahead after gaining material, the moved attacker is defended and attacks the blocker of a seventh-rank pawn; every enemy check permits a favorable checker capture and no enemy promotion is available
LEARNED queenless checking skewer: an equal-material low-material ending, a defended checking skewer, mobile king; no enemy check or immediate capture

LEARNED defensive equal-pawn activity: advance the king toward its pawn wing at equal material; no enemy passer, immediate forcing move, nearby undefended pawn, or doubled-pawn weakness. This is a defensive checkpoint, not a forced win. This checkpoint requires a quiet king move. Continue when the king attacks an enemy non-rook-file pawn.

EXPERIMENTAL queenless capture reserve: a queen capture gains at least two points with a minor-piece lead and mobile king; enemy checks allow equal-or-cheaper checker captures, no favorable enemy capture or immediate promotion. This is a bounded material-recovery heuristic, not a forced win.
LEARNED pawn opposition: an advancing king restricts the opposing king while keeping a positive paired-pawn race margin in an equal pawn ending, with no immediate enemy capture, check, or promotion

LEARNED defensive queen recovery: capture the enemy queen with check while retaining an unattacked queen, recover at least two material points to a one-pawn deficit, and retain an unconfined king with no enemy promotion; this is recovery, not a won-position certificate

LEARNED attacking queen-exchange recovery: an attacked cheaper piece captures the queen, leaving us one or two points ahead after gaining at least two points with our queen and three unconfined king flights; enemy has no queen or immediate promotion. The capturer may still be exchanged; this is a tactical recovery heuristic

LEARNED two-target initiative: while one pawn down, an attacked piece escapes to an unattacked square, attacks an equal-value piece, and uncovers another slider attack; retain our queen and unconfined king with no enemy check, strictly profitable capture, or promotion. This is an initiative heuristic, not a forced material win

LEARNED discovered-check initiative: an attacked piece captures an undefended target to recover equal material, escapes attack, opens a checking line and attacks a loose higher-valued rook; our queen and mobile king remain, and the opponent has no capture, countercheck or promotion. This is a two-threat initiative heuristic, not a forced-win proof

LEARNED pawn counterattack: a pawn captures to recover equal material, defends an attacked piece, attacks higher-valued material and opens another attacking line; retain our queen and unconfined king with no enemy favorable capture, check or promotion. This is a coordinated-activity heuristic, not a forced-win proof

LEARNED rook-skewer initiative: after gaining material, recapture an undefended target with a defended unattacked rook and create a skewer; retain our queen and three nonaligned king flights with no enemy check or promotion. This is an active-rook advantage heuristic and does not claim every en-prise piece is secured

states.label: Read the board
states.description: Choose a plan from present board facts. Initial read plus at most two rereads on a line. Tried plans are skipped on the same board.

rules.label: Secure newly gained material
A checking fork attacks a rook: begin with forcing or safe checks
Two effects in one legal move
After the king moves, collect an available higher-value target
Count the remaining material
A checking move is available
Without our queen, attack with the remaining pieces
A move attacks a rook and our nonpawn pieces are unattacked: examine targets and defenders
Use lines and pinned targets

states.label: Do two jobs
states.description: Look for one move with two named effects. The witnesses show both jobs.

rules.label: After creating a pin of more valuable material, follow the line and its defender replies
After a king move with equal material, examine targets and defenders
A king move now defends its queen: examine captures and pins along that line
With no opposing queen, follow the collection card

states.label: Attack the king
states.description: Examine captures that attack a rook and forcing checks, preferring checks that reduce king flights; then restrict the king or remove a defender.

states.label: Attack with the queen
states.description: Prefer checks answerable only by interposition and checking equal-or-better captures, then pawn threats, favorable captures, restrictive skewers, and supported checks.

states.label: Use a line
states.description: First recapture, then move a piece that was attacked while attacking the queen; then examine other captures and line tactics. The queen-threat cue does not assert that the destination is safe. Replies prioritize rook captures and moves of attacked pieces that defend another piece.

rules.label: An outside-square passer calls for a promotion plan
With equal material, follow a queen threat through queen exchanges and repairs

states.label: Targets and defenders
states.description: Answer king threats and exploit pins or safe checks, then consider a fork and collect material. When replying, defend the same rook that was attacked.

states.label: Collect material
states.description: Start with a more valuable or undefended target. Follow exchanges.

states.label: Repair a weakness
states.description: Answer check; move or defend the attacked piece, or exchange its attacker. After a king capture, finish collecting material.

rules.label: After a king capture, finish collecting material
After the opposing king moves with queens still opposing us, secure threatened material

states.label: Play an ending with pieces
states.description: Collect exposed pieces or use a skewer, keep the rook active, and support or stop passed pawns.

rules.label: Only kings and pawns remain

states.label: Offer a protected queen exchange
states.description: With equal material, first compare piece captures. Otherwise consider a protected queen exchange, checks, and captures. After a rook move, examine safe escapes first, sharing the repair procedure after other moves.

rules.label: After a non-rook move, continue with the shared repair procedure
Rescue an attacked knight, bishop, rook, or queen

states.label: Play the king and pawn ending
states.description: Collect a pawn, advance the king, restrict the opposing king, support an abreast pawn, defend loose pawns, then consider other king approaches.

rules.label: A promoted piece changes the ending

states.label: Rescue an attacked piece
states.description: When a piece is attacked, consider exchanging it for a piece, a check that opens a line, a protected capture, or safe defense.

rules.label: After this move, continue repairing until the next allowed board read

states.label: Find a safe check in the rook fork
states.description: Read a checking attack on a rook. Inspect checks requiring interposition, supported captures of pieces, then captures of unattacked nonpawn material. Continue with safe checks and equal-or-better exchanges. If no unattacked check remains, inspect defended checks. An enemy pawn on seventh redirects to forcing king attack.

rules.label: After trying the initial check, continue the two-jobs routine until another permitted board read
An enemy pawn is one step from promotion: keep a forcing king attack
An equal-or-better capture can collect the forked material
Without an unattacked check, combine threats or collect material

states.label: Start the rook fork
states.description: Start with forcing or safe checks. After the king moves, collect the forked material. With no checks available, continue with line targets.

rules.label: After trying the initial check, continue the two-jobs routine until another permitted board read
Enemy pawn near promotion: force the king first
After an enemy piece takes more valuable material, exploit the line
After an equal-or-greater capture with the opposing queen present, examine the line
After a noncapture that moves the king, opens a line, or escapes an attack, examine the forked material
With no opposing queen, answer a king attack on our rook through material counterplay
Without a check, continue with captures and line targets

proof.scope: Bounded tactical coverage within seven plies. Checkmate endpoints are verified from legal moves. All non-mate stopping checklists, including favorable pawn endings and the queen reserve, are material or positional heuristics, not forced-win certificates. Full official-line completion describes the recorded accepted path; later conversion can remain heuristic. Engine audits are separate from runtime decisions.
proof.replies: On each card, retain at most four unique opponent replies in stated predicate order and require all retained replies to succeed (AND). Unselected legal replies are not proved. Own choices are OR with at most four per plan. No engine result or puzzle answer enters runtime selection.
proof.reads: Initial board read plus at most two new idea reads per line, with separate sibling state; the global limit of 100 reached positions never resets. Child-availability facts are derived from complete generated legal candidates; generation is distinct from exploration.
